inferred_requirements.title: Authentication Platform Core
inferred_requirements.description: The system must provide authentication capabilities to verify user identities.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt 'Build an authentication platform'.

inferred_requirements.title: Token Revocation Mechanism
inferred_requirements.description: The system must support the ability to revoke issued authentication tokens.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt 'with token revocation'.

inferred_requirements.title: Token Blacklist or Validation State Store
inferred_requirements.description: The system must maintain a state store (such as a revocation list or blacklist) to verify if an incoming token has been explicitly invalidated prior to its natural expiration.
inferred_requirements.justification: Why 1: Stateless tokens (e.g., JWTs) remain valid until expiration by design, creating a security risk upon logout or compromise. Why 2: A stateful lookup mechanism (e.g., revocation cache, token ID blacklist, or incremented token versioning) must intercept validation flows to check revocation status. Why 3: No token marked as revoked can ever be successfully accepted for authenticated operations.

inferred_requirements.title: Token Format and Cryptographic Standard
inferred_requirements.description: The specific token format (e.g., JWT, PASETO) and signing algorithm (e.g., Ed25519, RS256, HS256) are unstated.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify the token standard, cryptographic algorithms, or transport protocols.

inferred_requirements.title: Storage Backend and Persistence Provider
inferred_requirements.description: The underlying database or persistence engine for user credentials and revocation state is unstated.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify database engines (e.g., PostgreSQL, Redis, DynamoDB) for storing state.
